messages.subject: Re: Model Equation
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I did use CFG with hidden layer=9 and activation function as tanh. It is giving me the desired result!
I need the model equation!
I am not trying to tune parameters of a neural network through GA but I am trying Multi-Response Optimization with help of desirability function and GA approach!
In essence, when I have more than one response variable(Y1,Y2,Y3) I want to predict the Xi's !!!

I am using the package desirability in R and GA in R.
For your reference I am attaching a paper related to this. Would you like to suggest me packages for GA that I must use in this case!
Thanks a lot for your reply!
I would be looking forward again for your reply intensely!

Thanking You,
Abhishek Das

On Fri, Sep 1, 2017 at 4:17 AM, Christoph Bergmeir <christoph...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi,
>
> that depends on things such as the activation function. If you use the logistic function and one hidden layer, it will be something like
>
> METs = ((1/(1 + EXP(9.18694*((VM − 4027.474318)/3153.286042) +
> 12.9723))* − 3.05383 + 1/(1 + EXP(1.8487*(VM-4027.474318) + 2.55011))*
> − 1.19096 + 1/(1 + EXP(3.84729*(VM − 4027.474318) + 4.11932))*1.24936))*2.303
> 724 + 3.733038
>
> Here, VM is an input and all the other values are weights that you want to optimize with your GA.
>
> This is from my following paper:
> https://scholar.google.com/citations?view_op=view_citation&hl=en&user=_UG_SgUAAAAJ&citation_for_view=_UG_SgUAAAAJ:roLk4NBRz8UC
>
> However, I don't think that using a GA will give you much better results. You could use the Conjugate Gradient implemented in SNNS instead of the Backprop that you probably use at the moment (that's a parameter of the function). Or, you give the nnet package a try that uses BFGS. It also shouldn't be too difficult to modify nnet to use a genetic algorithm instead of the BFGS. In RSNNS that will be more difficult, as it is more complex and all in C++. As a GA I recommend you our package Rmalschains, or maybe rgenoud. So, you could try to replace the BFGS in nnet with Rmalschains. That should work, but as I said, I doubt that the results will improve much.
>
> Regards,
> Christoph
>
>

> >
> > I have built a model using RSNNS mlp() function which has around 13

> > find a way to find that equation which would be my fitness function for GA.
> > Please help me on this issue its very urgent!
> >
> > Thanks,
> > Abhishek Das

messages.subject: Re: Model Equation
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

well, the equation will look more or less like the example I sent you,
but with tanh instead of the logistic function. Maybe you find some more
information in the SNNS user manual. Regarding the genetic algorithm,
package GA is probably fine, but it may be a bit slow as it is a pure R
implementation. But if your objective function is implemented in R it
won't make a big difference I suppose.

Regards,
Christoph
